Judgment delivered on 12.09.2024  CRMP No. 1437 of 2024
Mohammad Aslam Khan S/o Mohammad Ajaz Khan Aged About 40  Years R/o Housing Board Colony, Supela, Bhilai, Tehsil and District-  Durg, C.G.

... Petitioner  versus  State of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer, Police Station-  Vaishali Nagar, Durg Tehsil And District- Durg, C.G.
 ---- Respondent
For Petitioner : Mr. Anmol Sharma, Advocate For Respondent-State : Mr. Kishanlal Sahu, Dy. GA.
This petition has been filed under Section 482 of Cr.PC with the following prayers :-

2. That this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to allow this instant petition and quash the impugned orders dated 07.02.2024, 08.02.2024, 20.03.2024 and 09.04.2024 passed by the Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fourth F.T.S.C, (POCSO Act) Durg,
District Durg, C.G. in Special Criminal Case (POCSO) 160/2022.

Relevant facts for disposal of this petition is that complainant (mother of victim)
lodged report in concerned Police Station mentioning therein that petitioner forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her minor daughter, a deaf and dumb, as a result she became pregnant.

Based upon which, FIR was registered against petitioner/accused for offence punishable under Sections 376-A, 376 (2) (f) (j) (1) (d)
& 506 (B) IPC and Section 5,6, 5k of the Protection of Children From sexual offence Act, 2012 (for short 'the Act of 2012'); petitioner was arrested on 11.10.2022.

sentences.text: During course of investigation
, statement of witnesses were recorded, medical documents and other relevant documents were seized.
On completion of investigation, the prosecution filed charge sheet before the trial Court and petitioner was put to trial.

3. During pendency of trial, on 05.02.2024, prosecution has filed an application under Section 65 (b) of the Indian Evidence Act and sought permission to adduce secondary evidence in shape of duplicate copy of CT scan report of the victim which was conducted on 01.07.2022 on the ground that original is misplaced by complainant/mother of victim.
Accused opposed said application by filing reply.

By the order dated 7.2.2024, trial Court allowed the application filed under Section 65 (b) of the Evidence Act recording that CT scan report is an important document for proper adjudication of matter and as the original, which was given on suprudnama to complainant, is lost by her, therefore, in the interest of justice, it would be proper to take second copy on record and to grant permission to prove the same as a secondary evidence.
After passing of order dated 7.2.2024, prosecution moved an application under Section 311 CrPC for recalling of investigating officer for marking of secondary evidence as exhibit.
This application was also opposed by petitioner.
However, the trial Court vide order dated 8.2.2024 allowed the application under Section 311 CrPC for the reason mentioned therein.

4. On 18.03.2024, an application under Section 311 of Cr.PC was moved on behalf of accused/petitioner herein for re-examination of complainant (mother of victim) on the secondary evidence as also on other documents of Court proceeding relating to complainant.

The Court below considering that earlier permission to examine the complainant in respect of the documents filed on behalf of accused/petitioner has already been rejected, vide order dated 20.3.2024 denied permission to recall the complainant for re-examination on the said point recording that there is no need of summoning complainant for re-examination, however, permitted re-examination of Mohammad Aslam Khan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74127519/
2 complainant on the point of secondary evidence adduced by the prosecution.

sentences.text: Thereafter, petitioner moved another application for examination of signature of doctor appearing in CT Scan report, Article A-12, by a handwriting expert and to adduce opinion of handwriting expert as evidence.

The trial Court vide order dated 09.04.2024 rejected said application on the ground that though second copy of CT Scan report filed on behalf of prosecution has been taken on record but xerox of CT Scan already available in record has been marked as exhibit in the shape of secondary evidence, hence, there is no need of sending document Ex. A-12 for opinion of handwriting expert.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused submits that trial Court allowed the applications filed on behalf of prosecution in a mechanical manner without considering the objection raised on behalf of petitioner.

He submits that at the stage of judgment, the applications filed on behalf of prosecution were allowed by the trial Court, which is not permissible, as the same amounts to filling up the lacuna, which was left by prosecution, or to the disadvantage of the accused or to cause serious prejudice to the defence of the accused.

He further submits that if alleged signature of doctor on second copy of CT Scan report is examined by a handwriting expert and opinion is received, it would be easier for the trial Court to have an opinion about the truth and genuineness of alleged signature of doctor on it.
Such an expert opinion would give much more clarity for arriving at just decision in the matter.
Hence, the trial Court ought to have, as a matter of prudence, allowed the application for recall of complainant and for obtaining expert opinion.
He further submits that application for recall of witness filed on behalf of petitioner has been rejected by the trial Court on the technical ground that earlier similar request has been rejected.
He submits after examining of a witness, if in available circumstances, his/her evidence is necessary then the Court may recall such witness and record the evidence.

The documents based on which re-cross examination of the complainant is sought, are material to prove innocence of petitioner i.e. false implication, so in this regard the re-examination of said witnesses is necessary, therefore, the application ought not to have rejected by trial Court.
Rejections of applications of petitioner/accused in the given facts and circumstances of case would amount to failure of justice and also abuse of process of the Court.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner and stated that the learned trial Court rightly allowed applications filed by the prosecution to secure the fair justice in trial.
It is well settled that the provisions of Section 311 Cr.P.C. have been couched in wide terms and apply to any stage of all proceedings, inquiries and trial under CrPC.

He further submits that in the available scenario, as mentioned in the impugned orders,
the trial Court has not committed any error in dismissing request of petitioner for recall of witness and obtaining opinion of expert.
As such, the impugned order being based on proper appreciation of the factual matrix, is in accordance with law and does not require any interference at this stage.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for parties, perused the order-sheets of trial Court as well as other relevant material/evidence available on record.
8. So far as application of prosecution dated 05.02.2024 is concerned.

On perusal of order-sheets of trial Court, it is appearing that the sessions trial was at the final hearing stage and at that point of time, application dated 05.02.2024 was filed for adducing secondary evidence i.e. copy of CT Scan report, pleading that original was handed over to victim on suprudnama, retaining certified copy in record.
Said application was allowed by trial Court vide order dated 07.02.2024 and prosecution was permitted to adduced the secondary evidence.

Thereafter, an application under Section 311 CrPC was filed on behalf of prosecution for recalling Investigating Officer to mark exhibit on secondary evidence, which was also allowed on 08.02.2024 by the trial Court.

9. As per Section 65 (c) of the Evidence Act, "secondary evidence may be given of the existence, condition or contents of a document when the original has been destroyed or lost, or when the party offering evidence of its contents cannot, for any other reason not arising from his own default or neglect, produce it in reasonable time".

Thus it is clear that in case a party, seeking to tender secondary evidence, is unable to tender the original document, the same having been lost or destroyed, the Court may admit the certified copy of original as secondary evidence.

In case at hand, admittedly the original of CT Scan report was produced before the trial Court and after keeping certified copy of the same in record, the original was returned on suprudnama to the complainant.
The prosecution sought to tender secondary evidence on the ground that complainant is unable to tender original document as the same is lost.

Such being the position, in the considered view of this Court, the trial Court has not committed any mistake is allowing the prosecution application dated 05.02.2024 and admitted the certified copy of CT Scan report, which was already on record, into evidence.
10. It is also not in dispute that document which was marked as exhibit based on secondary evidence, is already a part of charge sheet and it is certified copy of CT Scan report.
In such a situation, the Investigating Officer was required to be recalled for getting the said document exhibited.
Thus, in the considered opinion, the trial Court has not committed any error in passing the order dated 08.02.2024 allowing application under Section 311 CrPC filed on behalf of the prosecution.

11.So far as applications dated 18.03.2024 & 06.04.2024 filed by the defence (petitioner herein) for recalling the complainant/mother of victim and summoning expert opinion with respect to signature of Doctor appearing in secondary evidence (CT scan report), is concerned, admittedly the Court is having ample powers to recall any witness at any stage of the proceeding subject to the condition that Court is satisfied that the same is material for just and proper disposal of the case.

Perusal of orders of trial Court dated (20.03.2024 & 09.04.2024) would reveal that secondary Mohammad Aslam Khan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74127519/

sentences.text: evidence allowed to be produced on record has not been marked as exhibit, rather the copy of CT Scan already in record of the Court has been marked as exhibit by comparing it from report adduced as secondary evidence.

Hence, it was not necessary either to recall the complainant/mother of victim to test the veracity of her statement that she lost the medical evidence or to send secondary evidence i.e. second copy of CT Scan report, for obtaining opinion of any handwriting expert with respect to signature of the doctor appearing thereon.

12.As regards the prayer for recall of complainant/mother of victim, for cross-examination on the documents of Court proceedings related to her is concerned, this prayer has already been considered and rejected by the trial Court vide order 02.12.2023 by which prayer of petitioner to take the aforementioned documents on record was allowed but prayer to cross-examine the complainant has been refused on the ground that she has already been examined and cross-examined earlier.

Needless to mention here that petitioner is facing trial for commission of offence of rape with a deaf and dumb girl, whereas the documents on which cross- examination is sought by petitioner relate to proceeding initiated by her against her husband, which appears to be irrelevant for determination of present case.

Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the orders impugned passed by trial Court do not suffer from any illegality or irregularity warranting interference in exercise of inherent jurisdiction of this Court.
13.For the foregoing discussion and observation, the petition stands dismissed.
No order as to cost.

-
Sd (Arvind Kumar Verma) Judge J/-
